scores.evidence: Receiver verifies the request, saves it and returns 202 within 10 s (GitHub's webhook timeout).
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (HMAC, delivery ID idempotency, installation tokens, no workflows permission) are accurate; minor issues like contents:write limited to agent/* by branch rules and 'approve' flow details are not wrong enough to matter.

scores.evidence: Trigger rule: an attempt starts only after a maintainer applies the `agent:attempt` label, or policy marks the category autonomous.
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolution with explicit deferrals and reasons, a buildable phased scope, and sensible ambiguity resolution.

scores.evidence: The model can only propose typed actions; a separate executor holds the GitHub token, checks each action against policy
scores.rationale: Consistent ledger/executor/policy design; small loose ends such as label autonomy vs gated comments and sandbox tools vs executor are minor.

scores.evidence: Replay eval harness, built first because it is the yardstick for everything else... score with the tests from the real fix, which are hidden
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks (red-team suite, egress tests, shadow mode, replay eval, exit checks per phase), with thresholds labeled as provisional, though post-launch regression monitoring is mostly via scorecards.

scores.evidence: Assumptions (none were given): GitHub.com, one org, a mix of private and public repos... If any of these is wrong, re-check gates G1, G6 and G7.
scores.rationale: Assumptions and revisit triggers are explicit and thresholds marked as starting targets, but some numbers (50 concurrent jobs, 10k queue depth) are unjustified.

scores.evidence: The reconciler repairs a manually injected half-finished action... cleanup also runs on crash; job resumes from ledger checkpoint
scores.rationale: Covers injection, duplicates, partial failures, eval poisoning, memory poisoning, flaky tests, loops, provider outages with concrete handling.

scores.evidence: GitHub Actions builds the image (pinned by digest), runs terraform apply to staging, then to prod after a smoke test
scores.rationale: Deployment, monitoring, alerts, kill switches, and reconciler are concrete; ownership/incident response and rollback details are thin.

scores.evidence: Resolution: ≤ 40 tool iterations, ≤ $3 per attempt, ≤ 30 min wall clock... Per-repo daily cap and an org-wide monthly cap.
scores.rationale: Caps, cost per job tracking, tiered models and buy vs build are covered, but no overall run or build cost estimate and the budget figures are ungrounded.

scores.evidence: Ledger schema... Every later capability writes through it, so it is the most expensive thing to get wrong.
scores.rationale: Identifies one-way decisions (ledger, triage schema, keying on provider/org/repo), isolates model behind interface, offers revisit triggers and exit paths for buy decisions.

scores.evidence: Modular monolith... One forced split: the sandbox executor is a separate, isolated runtime. That split is a security boundary
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with Postgres queue, single agent loop and explicit deferrals; the six-phase, nine-part AI layer is somewhat heavy for a modest team.

scores.evidence: Exit check: a real issue in prod gets the comment. One trace shows all five spans... Redelivering the same webhook... produces no second comment.
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified ordering, concrete first slice, checkable exit criteria at each phase and adaptation triggers.

checklist.evidence: Forbidden: merge, close, push to the default branch, workflow or settings changes.
No `workflows` permission, so the App cannot change CI at all. Short-lived installation tokens.
The model can only propose typed actions; the executor checks each one against policy.
an ephemeral microVM per job. No secrets. Network egress denied except a proxy that allows only package registries
The body contains the reproduction, root-cause summary, test evidence, trace link and an "AI-generated" label.
offline type-label accuracy ≥ 85% top-1. Duplicate precision ≥ 90% at recall ≥ 50%.
PR merged / merged-with-edits / closed, review comments... Promote one action class at a time per repo, based on scorecards
A single feature flag that stops all GitHub writes. It exists from commit one.
≤ 40 tool iterations, ≤ $3 per attempt, ≤ 30 min wall clock
full job replay possible from ledger (inputs, model version, prompt hash)
agentic search tools inside the sandbox (`ripgrep`, tree-sitter symbol lookup, file reads)

traps.evidence: The agent never merges, never closes issues and never pushes to default branches.
The token never enters model context or the sandbox.
the system prompt states it is never instructions.
a deliberately looping test task is cut off at the iteration cap

note: Strong, security-first phased plan with a concrete first slice, policy/ledger boundary and replay evals; weaknesses are thin ops ownership/rollback, ungrounded cost totals, and no explicit index freshness.
